findings.title: Revert of security fix reintroduces API-key leak risk via raw httpx exception logging
findings.why_it_matters: The loguru redacting sink (triggarr/logging.py) only strips exact, unmodified occurrences of known secret strings from the final formatted text. A URL-encoded, case-folded, or otherwise transformed copy of an API key embedded in an exception's rendered URL would not match and would reach stderr and the web UI log viewer buffer unredacted. This is precisely the scenario the original security fix (and the parallel _sanitize_exc mechanism used throughout engine.py/scheduler.py/routes.py) was built to close; reverting it here reopens that path in the one place it had already been fixed.

agent_notes: The two changed hunks undo the sanitization convention documented in triggarr/search/engine.py:30-35 ('Avoids storing raw str(exc) which may contain internal paths, URLs, or API keys that bypass the loguru redacting sink'). The removed code matched that convention.

Raw `exc=exc` logging does exist elsewhere (config.py, state.py, changelog.py, update_check.py, routes.py:613/808), but only for local file-I/O or settings-validation errors. Every *arr HTTP/response error path uses the sanitized form, so the convention applies by error source, and these hunks are HTTP/response errors.

Layering: _sanitize_exc lives in triggarr/search/engine.py, and clients/base.py sits below search. Importing it into base.py would make clients depend on search, which is an upward dependency. Moving it into a lower-level module (e.g. a triggarr/clients helper) would let base.py, tracking.py and engine.py share one implementation. Right now there are 3 copies of the same HTTP-status summarizing logic (engine.py:36-37, base.py:71-75, tracking.py:70-71), which meets the rule of three. This is not emitted as a separate finding because the copies predate this diff.
No tests in tests/ assert on these log message strings, so the change has no test coupling.

The security lane should look at the same sites, since the change touches the CLAUDE.md 'No API keys in logs' convention. The API key travels in the X-Api-Key header, not the URL, so a key leak through str(HTTPStatusError) depends on the base_url carrying credentials. Pending: confirm whether user-configured URLs can contain userinfo or query-string keys.
